A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, and their main text, equations, tables and proof appendices support comparison. However, v3 pages 33–34 contain only external-image notices for training and validation cluster-distribution plots, preventing comparison of those figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original MIMIC-IV experiments predicting mortality and length of stay, including oracle and specialized-expert results, allocation statistics and four-run uncertainty estimates.

after.justification: v3 reports original Pascal VOC object-detection experiments and revised MIMIC-IV experiments comparing its rejector with existing L2D methods.

M1.justification: The frozen-agent training procedure, rejector and weighted-surrogate construction remain. The substantive refinement replaces explicitly additive classification/regression costs with a general joint discrepancy function and instantiates detection-specific costs. The shared-backbone notation and added pseudocode do not independently establish a new routing architecture.

E1.justification: v3 adds Pascal VOC image-level object detection, coupling category prediction and localization. MIMIC-IV mortality and length-of-stay tasks remain, but the oracle scenario disappears and specialized experts now have different expertise across classification and regression. The isolated CIFAR-100 caption in Appendix G.1 conflicts with its Pascal VOC context and does not establish another evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: v1 reports model, expert and combined-system performance without evaluating competing L2D algorithms. v3 Table 1 adds the classification-focused Mao et al. (2023a) and regression-focused Mao et al. (2024e) rejectors to the EHR comparison. The latter work was cited as Mao et al. (2024b) in v1.

E3.justification: The specialized EHR rejector changes from 75 epochs, AdamW and learning rate 0.001 to 100 epochs, Adam, learning rate 0.003 and cosine scheduling. Checkpoint selection changes from allocation-confusion-matrix performance to minimum validation risk, and v3 describes separate task transformers. New detection protocols introduce mAP and computation-scaled expert costs. The 5,995-sample MIMIC-IV dataset and 80/20 split remain.

E4.justification: The EHR oracle query-cost sweep and specialized-expert allocation confusion-matrix analysis are removed. v3 adds a Pascal VOC cost-sensitivity study examining transitions between the model and two experts with different computational costs. This substantially revises the questions and evidence concerning allocation behavior.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across four runs or trials. v3 removes v1's explicit seed-42 selection and subsequent model-retraining account, and its individual-agent tables present point estimates instead of the earlier uncertainty entries. There is no stated increase in trial count.

E6.justification: The EHR system result changes from 71% accuracy and 1.09 sL1 in v1 Table 3 to 70.0% and 1.28 in v3 Table 1, under changed expert and training conditions, so this is not a same-setting performance comparison. v3 adds baseline results and detection results, including 44.2% mAP at beta2 = 0.15, while removing oracle and confusion-matrix entries.

T1.justification: v3 replaces the independence-based composite-loss formalization with joint-model and general-cost definitions, revises Theorem 4 using cross-entropy-specific inverse transformations, and adds Theorem 6's parameter-dependent minimizability-gap characterization and Appendix D proof. The earlier composite-loss consistency lemma is removed. The Rademacher generalization-bound formula is retained after renumbering.

C1.justification: v3 makes tight surrogate-specific bounds and multi-expert minimizability-gap generalization central contributions. It also claims existing L2D methods fail for coupled object detection and can be suboptimal on EHR tasks, whereas v1 primarily claims improvements over its underlying model. The consistency guarantee is now framed around cross-entropy surrogates rather than arbitrary multiclass surrogates admitting consistency bounds.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations connecting surrogate parameters and cost distributions to minimizability gaps, and computational costs to expert selection. Its EHR discussion emphasizes balancing competing task metrics and reducing expert involvement, replacing v1's emphasis on base-model improvement and allocation correctness. It explains differing expertise across tasks as a source of suboptimal single-task deferral.

D1.justification: v3 adds Algorithm 1, NVIDIA H100 hardware information and detection-specific training details. Conversely, it drops v1's detailed EHR pretraining recipe, parameter counts, dropout settings, numerical task-cost weights and regression-loss bound. These additions and omissions substantially change reproducibility information; both versions continue to state that their implementation is available.

R1.justification: v3 expands the learning-with-abstention background and introduces recent work on enhanced H-consistency, realizable consistency and abstention minimizability gaps. It positions its bounds and gap analysis as improvements or generalizations of those results, while removing several earlier general multi-task and regression references. Existing Mao deferral papers remain despite changed citation suffixes.

P1.justification: The abstract, contributions, related work, preliminaries and theoretical exposition are extensively rewritten. Experiments are reorganized by application rather than expert type, and the former two-part appendix with a contents page becomes Appendices A–G, beginning with an algorithm. These are substantial narrative and organizational revisions.

P2.justification: The visible experimental presentation is substantially redesigned: v3 introduces a two-panel detection performance/allocation plot, a comparative EHR table, detection-result tables and an algorithm block, while removing the oracle and confusion-matrix displays and restructuring agent tables. Changes to the cluster-distribution figures themselves remain unknown because v3 supplies notices instead of embedded images.

improvement.justification: Detection experiments and direct L2D baselines substantially strengthen v1's limited empirical validation. However, reproducibility details are lost, and a central new theorem has a substantive error: for nu = 3 and two unit aggregated costs, Theorem 6 claims minimum risk 0.75, while Appendix D Equation 24 gives 0.59 at softmax probabilities (0.9, 0.1). Thus the added theory is not valid over its stated range. These empirical gains and theoretical and documentation harms prevent a confident net quality judgment.
